\begin{minipage}{\textwidth}\footnotesize
\textit{Notes.} Coefficients on the log-odds scale; standard errors in parentheses. $^{*}$p$<$0.1; $^{**}$p$<$0.05; $^{***}$p$<$0.01. Firth columns: penalised-likelihood logit (rare events), $p$-values from the penalised likelihood-ratio test. Universe: the place universe of Table~\ref{tab:descriptives}, less places without 2020 vote data (Alaska, Hawaii, and places with no reallocated returns) or without LEHD employment ratio or retail/food job share; every column uses this sample. Full specification: the place adoption model of Table~\ref{tab:crosslevel-adoption} without change in white share, which is not yet built for this sample, plus camera exposure and county also restricted. The omitted race category is everyone not Black, Hispanic or Asian. Camera exposure enters as both margins of the hurdle: whether the place has any mapped camera, and how many. Descriptive associations, not causal effects. Full specification in every column. Outcome in every column: any restriction (Table~\ref{tab:ban-models}, column 1), redefined as follows. (1) Drops decisions that followed a state law or order (Table~\ref{tab:ban-counts}). (2) Drops partial actions --- those covering only some cameras, only new installations, or only cameras on state roads. (3) Keeps only decisions whose source states the action and date explicitly (high confidence). (4) Drops decisions about a vendor other than Flock Safety. (5) Restricts the sample to places with at least one mapped camera, the risk set for reversal.
\end{minipage}
